subject: Permission inventory & SAML/SCIM evidence for SIG scope
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Lin <tara.lin@alphamed.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Permission inventory & SAML/SCIM evidence for SIG scope

Hi Tara —

Thanks again for the quick SIG intake call yesterday. AlphaMed’s security team asked us to provide a compact set of artifacts to scope SSO/SCIM/RBAC controls for the SIG questionnaire. To keep the package small for initial review, can you send the following: 

- A redacted SAML assertion sample for a typical end-user login (include AttributeStatement names).
- A recent SCIM delta export (one-week window) or a CSV extract showing provisioning events.
- A condensed RBAC role matrix (owner, admin, end-user) — a spreadsheet is fine.

If you have a preferred location to upload (SecureShare, DocuSign, S3 link with expiry), send that and we’ll pull artifacts from there. If easier, you can attach the three files directly to the reply — small redactions are fine.

Target for our team to hand AlphaMed the SIG evidence pack: EOD Wednesday 2025-12-10. If you need more time, let me know and we’ll propose a brief extension.

Thanks,
Karthik
---
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Tara Lin <tara.lin@alphamed.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@alphamed.com
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Permission inventory & SAML/SCIM evidence for SIG scope

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear checklist. Attached are the items we can share immediately:

- saml-assertion-sample.xml (PII redacted; contains NameID, email, department attributes) [Attachment: saml-assertion-sample.xml (text/xml)]
- scim-sync-log-202511.csv (contains provisioning events for 2025-11-20 to 2025-11-27) [Attachment: scim-sync-log-202511.csv (text/csv)]
- rbac-role-matrix-compact.xlsx (role -> permission mapping, redacted service accounts) [Attachment: rbac-role-matrix-compact.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

We’re uploading the same bundle to our SecureShare link in case your reviewer prefers download instead of email: https://secureshare.alphamed.com/drop/AM-SIG-2025-12-09 (expires 2025-12-16).

Quick notes on the artifacts:
- The SAML assertion includes an example of a delegated-portal role claim — that should show group-to-role mapping.
- SCIM export is a snapshot of delta events; let us know if you need full history and we can schedule a signed transfer.
- RBAC matrix omits treatment of system service accounts for this tranche; we can provide a separate workbook if you need service-account entitlements.

If you want a short walkthrough call to orient your reviewer to the SCIM columns, I’m available tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Tara
Tara Lin
Information Security Manager
AlphaMed
T: 617-555-0199
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Permission inventory & SAML/SCIM evidence for SIG scope

Forwarding AlphaMed’s package from Tara — attachments are PII-redacted and the SecureShare link is included (expires 2025-12-16).

Action items for our SIG pack (please coordinate directly):
1) Soojin — review the SAML assertion sample and extract the list of AttributeStatement names and example values. I want an explicit mapping back to our identity attributes used in production (Attr -> Redwood claim mapping).
2) Grace — verify the SCIM CSV columns map to our provisioning schema and call out any gaps (e.g., lack of lastModified iso8601 timestamps).
3) Both — take the RBAC matrix and confirm role names align with our canonical role registry; flag any role name collisions or overly permissive assignments.

Course of action: curate a one-page cover memo that summarizes findings (one-paragraph risk note per artifact) and attach the original artifacts. We’ll upload the curated bundle to the SIG portal and note any asks for follow-up evidence.

ETA: EOD Wednesday (2025-12-10) for the memo and completed checks. If we can’t meet EOD, ping me with a short extension request.

Cheers,
Karthik

ACK — I pulled the attachments from SecureShare and started a quick pass. First-pass notes: 
- SAML assertion: attributes look standard (email, name, dept); will map claims to our identity attrs and flag any mismatch.
- SCIM CSV: lastModified present but in epoch ms for some rows — I’ll normalize and call that out in the memo.
- RBAC matrix: a few role names don’t match our canonical registry (I’ll annotate directly in the spreadsheet).

I’ll have the one-page cover memo and the annotated spreadsheet by EOD Friday 2025-12-12; if we want to stick to the original EOD Wednesday target I can re-prioritize but may need an extra engineer to help with CSV normalization.

Will follow up with the memo and an upload link.

Thanks,
Soojin
